plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled flowers on bare branches in the cold of late winter. It is widely cultivated as an ornamental and for its fruit, which is pickled or made into liqueur.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Japan, China, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are celebrated in East Asia as a symbol of perseverance because they bloom while snow may still be on the ground, and ume viewing parties often precede cherry blossom season.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It carpets woodlands and gardens, often pushing up through snow and frost.
plants.location: Europe, naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops contain galantamine, a compound that has been developed into a medication for treating symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A shrub bearing the largest flower head in the Protea genus, a large cup of showy pink bracts surrounding a center of fuzzy flowers. It grows in fynbos vegetation on nutrient-poor, well-drained soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, with peak flowering in late summer to autumn, and some blooms from midsummer
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its flower heads can reach up to 30 cm across; the genus is named for the Greek god Proteus, who could change shape.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers in many forms, from single to fully double. It thrives in mild, humid climates and blooms when little else is in flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring (December to April)
plants.location: Japan, Korea, China; widely grown in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and its seeds yield camellia oil used for cooking and hair care in Japan.
